hook.line: In Bogotá, half of all conversation is a hunch you can't prove, and *chismes* travel fast. Tomás needs a way to say "I suspect" without swearing to it.
hook.es: Para mí que aquí pasa algo raro.
hook.en: If you ask me, something odd is going on here.

examples.en: If you ask me, something odd is going on here.

examples.en: If you ask me, he doesn't know anything.

rule:
*Para mí que* opens a hunch: something you suspect but can't prove. English says "If you ask me" or "I bet".

What follows is a normal sentence with a normal verb: *no sabe*, *va a quedar*, *está*. No special mood, because you believe it.

It is casual, friends-at-the-café talk. *Para mí* on its own means "in my view"; add *que* when a full sentence follows.
smallPrint: Teachers call *para mí que* an opinion marker. It takes the plain verb form (the indicative), since the speaker is fairly sure.

readAndPick.es: Para mí que mañana no abren.
options: If you ask me, they are opening tomorrow.
If you ask me, they aren't opening tomorrow.
If you ask me, they didn't open yesterday.

readAndPick.es: Para mí que Tomás se va a quedar.
options: If you ask me, Tomás is going to leave.
If you ask me, Tomás is going to stay.

readAndPick.es: Para mí que Vale está cansada.
options: If you ask me, Vale was tired.
If you ask me, Vale isn't tired.
If you ask me, Vale is tired.

readAndPick.es: Para mí que aquí pasa algo raro.
options: If you ask me, something odd is going on here.
If you ask me, nothing odd is going on here.
If you ask me, something odd happened here.

readAndPick.es: Para mí que no sabe nada.
options: If you ask me, he knows everything.
If you ask me, he doesn't know anything.
If you ask me, he asked nothing.

readAndPick.es: Para mí que ellos ya lo saben.
options: If you ask me, they already know it.
If you ask me, I already know it.
If you ask me, they don't know it yet.

readAndPick.es: Para mí que ya se fue.
options: If you ask me, he is about to leave.
If you ask me, he never came.
If you ask me, he already left.

readAndPick.es: Para mí que Hernando sabe más de lo que dice.
options: If you ask me, Hernando says more than he knows.
If you ask me, Hernando knows more than he says.
If you ask me, Hernando knows less than he says.

yourTurn.prompt: Pick *Para mí* or *Para mí que* and type the whole sentence: ___ no sabe nada.
yourTurn.answer: Para mí que no sabe nada.
accept: Para mí que no sabe nada
yourTurn.why: A full sentence after the hunch needs *que*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: If you ask me, Tomás is going to stay.
yourTurn.answer: Para mí que Tomás se va a quedar.
accept: Para mí que Tomás va a quedarse.
yourTurn.why: Plain verb after *que*, just as in a normal sentence.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: If you ask me, Vale is tired.
yourTurn.answer: Para mí que Vale está cansada.
yourTurn.why: *Está cansada* stays as it is; the hunch is just the opener.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: If you ask me, the café isn't going to close.
yourTurn.answer: Para mí que el café no va a cerrar.
yourTurn.why: Put *no* before the verb inside the hunch.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it negative: *Para mí que mañana abren.* Say: If you ask me, they aren't opening tomorrow.
yourTurn.answer: Para mí que mañana no abren.
accept: Para mí que no abren mañana.
yourTurn.why: *No* goes right before *abren*, and *Para mí que* stays in front.

yourTurn.prompt: Say it about *ellos*: If you ask me, they already know.
yourTurn.answer: Para mí que ya lo saben.
accept: Para mí que ellos ya lo saben.
yourTurn.why: Only the verb changes to *saben*; the opener stays.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: If you ask me, Hernando knows more than he says.
yourTurn.answer: Para mí que Hernando sabe más de lo que dice.
yourTurn.why: *Más de lo que dice* is the Spanish way to say "more than he says".

pitfalls.wrong: Para yo que no sabe nada.
pitfalls.right: Para mí que no sabe nada.

pitfalls.wrong: Por mí que aquí pasa algo raro.
pitfalls.right: Para mí que aquí pasa algo raro.
pitfalls.why: Almost. The hunch opener is *para mí*; *por mí* means "as far as I'm concerned" in a different way.
Almost. It is a hunch you believe, so the verb stays plain: *es*.

personal: Say a hunch of your own about someone or something near you, starting with *Para mí que*.
